qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Direct-Store-Delivery (DSD) route density and retail shelf dominance across Frito-Lay salty snacks (~60% US market share) and beverages create an insurmountable distribution moat. 10Y median ROIC of 16.8% and gross margins stable at 53-55% prove moat durability. Primary erosion threats include GLP-1 adoption, health/wellness shifts away from ultra-processed snacks, and consumer resistance to cumulative price increases.
qualitative.note: Global snack and beverage powerhouse anchored by Frito-Lay's dominant DSD distribution network. Demonstrates durable pricing power and Lindy snack brand loyalty. High cash conversion (>85% FCF/NI) and steady balance sheet with >10x net interest coverage comfortably support capital returns. [5-10Y g: snack/beverage volume 1.0% + price 2.0% + international mix 1.5% - promotional/input cost drag 0.5% + net buybacks 1.0%]
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median ROIC of 16.8% and FY24/FY25 operating margins ~12-14%. Net revenue grew to $93.9B in FY25 with operating cash flow of $12.5B and FCF of $8.2B (99% FCF conversion). Net interest coverage remains strong at ~10x. Frito-Lay generates outsized operating profit share (~45-50% of corporate profit) providing high-margin stability.
